channel.title: Pass the Architect: CCAO-F
channel.description: A two-host study series for the Claude Certified Associate - Foundations exam: prompting, checking outputs, products and models, workflows, Projects, responsible use and troubleshooting. Follows the v1.0 exam guide (July 2026), for exams sat before 7 December 2026.
channel.itunes:summary: A two-host study series for the Claude Certified Associate - Foundations exam: prompting, checking outputs, products and models, workflows, Projects, responsible use and troubleshooting. Follows the v1.0 exam guide (July 2026), for exams sat before 7 December 2026.
channel.itunes:author: Pass the Architect

item.title: 09. Exam day
item.description: A short episode for the morning of the Associate Foundations exam: what to bring and the rules on the day, a noteboard built from the series method, how to read the countdown clock, the item formats, and what to do in the last ten minutes.

item.title: 08. Associate final drill
item.description: Thirty-five quick items across all seven Associate domains, weighted like the paper, then the wrong-answer families to strike on sight, the exam-day essentials in brief, and one last retrieval before you sleep.

item.title: 07. Troubleshooting and optimisation
item.description: Diagnose a poor output by finding what changed, match each symptom to its fix, turn feedback into a tested change, and streamline a repeated workflow without overspending.

item.title: 06. Governance, risk and responsible use
item.description: Sorting use cases by what happens when the output is wrong, sending only the data a task needs into an approved workspace, what to do when the AI policy is silent or something has gone wrong, and the ethics of bias, disclosure and accountability.

item.title: 05. Projects, knowledge and connectors
item.description: Setting up a Project with instructions and knowledge, choosing between uploaded files and connectors such as Google Drive and Gmail, writing project instructions that work, and keeping a shared configuration current.

item.title: 04. Bringing Claude into a workflow
item.description: Pulling requirements out of messy notes without settling the arguments, research and process optimisation that start from real detail, prototyping versus escalating, augmenting a step versus redesigning a process, and explaining Claude's value and limits to a sponsor.

item.title: 03. Choosing the product and the model
item.description: When to use chat, a Project, research or an artifact; how Haiku, Sonnet and Opus trade cost, speed and quality; and when a long conversation should be restarted, summarised or persisted.

item.title: 02. Checking what Claude gives you
item.description: The heaviest domain on the Associate paper: judging accuracy and completeness, catching invented details, contradictions and slanted framing, checking against the source, deciding when a person must review, adapting drafts for the reader, and choosing between inline, artifact and structured data.

item.title: 01. Prompting and task execution
item.description: How to write a prompt a capable newcomer could act on, break a big request into stages, iterate by changing one thing at a time, and adapt the approach for analysis, research, drafting and brainstorming.

item.title: 00. Associate game plan
item.description: How the Associate Foundations exam is built: sixty items, seven domain weights, countdown-clock pacing and dropdown items, and a four-step method for reading any item in plain business language, worked through the three official sample questions.
